text:
The Sabres finally stopped a five-game skid on Thursday in Washington, a 6-3 win where Jack Quinn scored twice and Rasmus Dahlin had two points. Two nights later they let a game with Florida slip in the last four minutes and lost 4-3. That is the season in miniature: competitive, often decent, and 9-10-4.

The underlying play is close to even. Buffalo has 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and an even split at 5-on-5, but it has scored about six fewer goals than those chances suggest. Noah Ostlund is the clearest case, with 3 points in his last 10 against 5.3 expected. His line with Quinn and Zach Benson has been the team's best, taking 59% of the expected goals and outscoring opponents 9-4. Tage Thompson's line with Peyton Krebs and Benson has gone 8-2.

In net, Alex Lyon is still looking for his first win at 0-3-1, a fact Bleacher Report's Joe Yerdon noted after Saturday's loss.

Our playoff odds have Buffalo at 17%, and 3-6-1 in the last 10 is why the number is that low. What we'd watch: whether the Quinn line keeps driving play, and whether a few of the missing goals finally start going in.
